note: Optimizations mmt perf-optimize accepted, as reusable patterns. symptom.when is a condition over a perf report's attribution row for one mod: every clause must hold, and a clause holds when the samples of the entries in `in` (methods, features or threads) whose name matches the regex `matches` are at least `minShare` of the mod's samples, or, for `in: threadCpu`, when the operating system's CPU time of the mod's threads whose names match is at least `minMsPerSecond` (time in native code, which samples barely see). mmt perf lists the patterns a capture's hotspots match. change is what was changed; gain is the measured speedup with its 95% interval for cold and warm captures; gate is the equivalence gate that proved the output unchanged; provenIn names the mod, version, loader, scope and the kept run in coverage/perf-runs.json. test holds two attribution rows: fires must match the symptom and quiet must not (self-test runs both).

symptom.text: A value derived per chunk snapshot (here biome tint blending) is recomputed far more often than chunks arrive, because every light or block update replaces the snapshot and drops what was derived from it.

patterns.change: When a chunk's snapshot is replaced, the new one adopts the old one's derived value if every input the derivation reads is identical: the same biome container objects for the chunk and its eight neighbours (the game swaps containers in rather than mutating them), the same column tops, zoom seed, blend radius and colour-resolver generation. Compare inputs by identity where the game guarantees immutability, by value otherwise, and copy before the snapshot becomes visible to workers.

gate.name: tints-live + bake-digest
gate.detail: every tint the live map holds after the flight equals a fresh blend of its snapshot; the bake functions' digest on frozen chunks is unchanged

symptom.text: A per-sample ray pass (here spawn-spot picking, one ray per map sample) runs over the whole tile on every bake, although most bakes are partial updates whose dirty blocks cover a fraction of it.

patterns.change: Start from the previous result and redo only the dirty blocks, when the previous result is known to come from the bake immediately before this one: keep, per tile, which bake produced the stored result (a sequence number), under which store, generation and ray start height, and fall back to the whole pass on any gap (a discarded bake, a load from disk, another start height, more dirty than the limit). Correctness rests on the dirty region covering every sample whose ray could change, which the mod's own partial updates already rely on; confirm it with an instrumented build that also runs the whole pass and counts differences.

gate.name: incremental equals whole pass (instrumented) + bake-digest
gate.detail: 444 incremental picks during the flight equal the whole pick; the bake functions' digest is unchanged

symptom.text: A list that changes only when a cache is rebuilt (here a pipe's connections) is sorted, streamed into a new list, on every use: every extraction of every pipe, every tick.

patterns.change: Keep the sorted copy (one per order) beside the list it was made from, and reuse it while the source is the same object: the connection cache is replaced, never changed in place, so identity says when to sort again. Keep orders that must differ per call (a shuffle) uncached, and return the shared copy unmodifiable so no caller can change it.

symptom.text: A position type stores its dimension as a string and parses it back into a registry key (ResourceLocation.tryParse, ResourceKey.create) on every capability or level lookup, and builds the string again for every offset position, thousands of times a tick.

patterns.change: Memoize the string-to-key and key-to-string conversions in static concurrent maps. ResourceKey.create interns its result, so the remembered key is the very object a fresh parse returns; still call server.getLevel(key) every time, so a level added or removed later is seen as before. Leave unparseable strings to the original path.

symptom.text: A network controller re-resolves every node of its network each tick (a capability lookup per node per kind: node, importer, exporter, processor), though only a few nodes act and the set changes only when blocks do.

patterns.change: Look the capabilities up through NeoForge BlockCapabilityCaches made with an invalidation listener, and keep the resolved node list (in the iteration order the per-tick HashSet gives) with each node's capabilities until the node set is replaced or a listener fires. Still check every position is loaded each tick (a chunk stops being loaded before its unload event), fall back to lookups for a node whose position moved, and to fresh lookups for the rest of a tick in which a cache is invalidated. A cache calls its listener only if it was queried since its last invalidation: query every cache a plan depends on when the plan is made. A lookup also reads the node's chunk through ServerChunkCache.getChunk(x, z, FULL, true), which renews a one-tick ticket: that is what keeps a network's chunks loaded while its controller ticks. Make that read once per tick for every chunk holding a node when the plan is used, and before every answer taken from a cache, or far chunks unload and the network shrinks.

symptom.text: Every cable method (insert, extract, count slots, list stacks) looks up its target inventory's item handler again, building a new wrapper each time, many times per transfer.

patterns.change: Keep one NeoForge BlockCapabilityCache of Capabilities.ItemHandler.BLOCK per cable for its target position and side, used only while the target is loaded (a fresh lookup would load the chunk), and remade when the target position, side or level differs. Cache only NeoForge's answers for vanilla barrels and chests (an exact InvWrapper of a BarrelBlockEntity, ChestBlockEntity or CompoundContainer; chests invalidate when they join or leave a double chest), because their chunk reads are known, and make those reads before returning a cached answer: getChunk on the target's chunk, and for a chest whose type is not SINGLE on the chunk of the half it points at. Look any other target up every time: a provider can read other chunks, renewing their tickets, and a cache would skip that.

symptom.text: An export or request batch first lists every slot of every storage that could provide (a simulated extract and a filter check per slot of thousands), then serves the requests from the list, although they are usually met by the first few providers.

patterns.change: Decide each provider just before it is used, in the same storage and slot order, and stop when every request for the item is met (count 0, after which each later provider would only simulate). Do it only when the answer cannot differ from the up-front list: every storage and export target is a plain vanilla barrel or chest (an exact InvWrapper, slots independent, no loot table left to unpack), no inventory is behind two storages and no export target is a storage; otherwise list everything first as before. Decide whether an export target is plain without reading its chunk (from a cache that already holds a vanilla barrel or single chest; otherwise list everything first): the unmodified mod reads an export's target only when items move, and a read every export would keep that chunk loaded.

symptom.text: A machine finds its recipe every tick by testing each recipe of a type in turn (often after RecipeManager.getAllRecipesFor, which copies the whole list on every call), although its inputs rarely change.

patterns.change: Keep the scan's answer per block entity with copies of the stacks it was computed from, and return it while every input slot holds an equal stack (ItemStack.matches: item, count, components; compare copies, so a stack changed in place is noticed) and the server's recipes are the same set: RecipeManager replaces its maps on every reload and replaceRecipes, so the identity of getRecipes() changes exactly then. Scan as before whenever an input holds a filled map: the map extending recipe is the one vanilla crafting recipe whose match reads the level (the map's saved data). Vanilla's own Crafter keeps a RecipeCache under the same rule.

symptom.text: A per-tick check copies every input and recipe slot into new lists, matches them against each other with removeAll, and throws the lists away; it runs every tick although it only decides whether a timer may count down.

patterns.change: Compute the same answer from the slots in place, with items and counts in small arrays and no stack copied. Keep every quirk of the list version: a stack whose count ran out reads as air and so matches empty slots, and a copied empty stack is the one ItemStack.EMPTY, so removeAll (identity) took every empty slot at once when it took one.

symptom.text: Every tick a block entity takes a display slot's stack out and puts an equal one back (a recipe preview, a ghost or result slot), and copies its grid into a crafting container, although neither changed.

patterns.change: Skip the write while the slot already holds an equal stack (ItemStack.matches) of its own, and copy the grid into the crafting container only when the recipe is looked up again (the copies made then stay equal to the grid). NeoForge's ItemStackHandler.insertItem keeps the very stack it is given in an empty slot, so the same object can sit in two slots: Cyclic's crafter puts the result stack in its preview and then in an empty output slot on a craft tick, and later crafts grow it there. Write exactly as before whenever the slot's object may be shared (the craft tick and the tick after), and skip only when it is a stack the slot alone holds.

symptom.text: A per-tile pass (here a GPU mesher walking every column of a map tile, its shadow casters, and a per-sample spawn-spot ray pass) dominates a mod's CPU, and the same tile is rebuilt many times as nearby chunks load, though most of its columns come out the same each time.

patterns.change: Keep, per tile, each column's output and exactly what it read: the chunks under the cells its rays reached (and their neighbours), each by a token that a replacement snapshot inherits only when its blocks (or light) are equal, plus derived inputs such as tint arrays and any saved data it consulted. Take a column again only when the tile's settings are equal and every recorded input matches; record outputs packed so a bounded LRU holds a flight's worth of tiles. The same works for a ray pass whose rays stay in their column. Compare a replacement snapshot with its predecessor on the first worker that asks, not on the client thread. Keep the per-column walk in its own method: new branches in a huge hot method trigger uncommon traps that send the whole method back to the interpreter.

gain.scope: live mapping CPU (decision metric: Diorama's baker threads and the render thread)

gate.name: reuse-live + bake-digest
gate.detail: every live tile meshed and its spots picked with each reuse switch off and twice on come out identical, and corrupting a kept record makes the gate fail; the bake functions' digest on frozen chunks is unchanged

symptom.text: A pass over a wide region around each tile (here shadow casters, scanned over dozens of chunks the neighbouring tiles scan too) recomputes from every chunk's blocks on every bake.

patterns.change: Work it out once per chunk content and keep it with the snapshot under a token that content-equal replacement snapshots inherit, so every bake of every tile over that chunk shares it. Store it as a few primitive arrays per chunk (an offset table and one packed array), built for the whole chunk at once: kept as one small object per column it was half a million long-lived objects, and every young collection took 3 ms longer.

gate.name: reuse-live + bake-digest
gate.detail: every live tile meshed and its spots picked with each reuse switch off and twice on come out identical, and corrupting a kept record makes the gate fail; the bake functions' digest on frozen chunks is unchanged

symptom.text: A cache of packed results kept for seconds between passes (here camera faces, shadow-caster rows and spawn-spot columns kept per tile column) is built as many small primitive arrays; the bakes got faster but every young collection got longer, because the kept arrays are copied from one survivor space to the next before they are promoted.

patterns.change: Copy what the cache keeps into a ring of a few arrays, each one collector region long (at least half a G1 region, so it is allocated in the old generation and never copied), allocated once and filled in turn; a kept record holds (array, offset, length, the pass that wrote it). Entries in a pass older than the ring are dropped, an entry about to leave is copied forward when it is taken again, and since an array is written over once it leaves the ring, every read is checked afterwards against the array's pass (a StampedLock-style validation) and the work is redone if it changed. Allocating a new large array whenever one filled started a young collection and a concurrent cycle each time; the ring allocates each once.

symptom.text: A mod's monitoring or statistics thread uses tens of milliseconds of CPU a second with almost no execution samples: its time is in native code. On Windows, OperatingSystemMXBean.getProcessCpuLoad() (and a JFR or JMX reading of it) queries a performance counter of every process on the machine, about 200 ms of CPU a call with a few hundred processes running.

patterns.change: Compute the process load from the process's CPU time: (getProcessCpuTime() now - at the last reading) / (nanoTime now - at the last reading) / availableProcessors, clamped to [0, 1], negative before a first reading, as getProcessCpuLoad() measures it since its last call. getProcessCpuTime() is one system call. Keep getProcessCpuLoad() when CPU time is unavailable (-1). Read the system load as before (cheap there).

symptom.text: Each entity's fluid pushing (or any per-entity, per-tick check) builds a map or array sized to a whole registry (Forge: new Object2ObjectArrayMap(FluidType.SIZE - 1), 759 fluid types in All the Mods 9, two 758-slot arrays a call) though a call holds a few entries: allocation in the millions of bytes a second that grows with the entity count, and young collections with it.

patterns.change: Start the per-call map empty (Object2ObjectArrayMap() shares fastutil's empty arrays) and let it grow as entries arrive; an array map keeps insertion order, so iterating it afterwards visits the same entries in the same order. In a mod, redirect the NEW of the pre-sized map (here a ModernFix mixin on Forge's Entity.updateFluidHeightAndDoFluidPushing(Predicate)).
